name: General Meeting Notes
instructions:
Sections (use exactly these headings, in this order):
## Overview
(2–4 sentence executive summary, then one line stating the main purpose of the meeting.)
## Key Discussion Points
(one bullet per topic: **topic in bold** followed by the main ideas, observations and relevant supporting context (sub-bullets allowed).)
## Decisions Made
(bullets.)
## Action Items
(a Markdown checklist: "- [ ] Task — Owner: … — Due: … — Priority: …" (omit Priority when not given).)
## Outstanding Questions
(bullets.)
## Next Steps
(bullets; only follow-ups, meetings or deadlines actually mentioned.)
## Important Quotes
(bullets: > "quote" — speaker [timestamp].)
## Detailed Meeting Notes
(a thorough chronological account, one ### subheading per topic with paragraphs or bullets capturing all substantive details.)

name: Executive Summary
description: One-page brief for leaders who were not there.
instructions:
Write for a busy executive who was not present. Keep the whole document under 350 words.
Sections (use exactly these headings, in this order):
## Bottom Line
(2–3 sentences: what this meeting means and what matters most.)
## Key Outcomes
(at most 5 bullets: decisions and conclusions.)
## Risks & Concerns
(bullets of risks, blockers or disagreements raised.)
## Asks & Owners
(bullets: what needs to happen and who owns it ("owner not specified" if unknown).)
## Timeline
(dates and deadlines actually mentioned.)

name: Staff Meeting
instructions:
Sections (use exactly these headings, in this order):
## Summary
(3 sentences.)
## Team Updates
(group updates by person or area/department when the transcript makes that clear; otherwise by topic. Bullets.)
## Announcements
(bullets.)
## Decisions
(bullets.)
## Assignments
(a Markdown table with columns: Task | Owner | Due | Notes. Use "—" for unknown values.)
## Calendar & Deadlines
(dates and events mentioned.)
## Items for Next Meeting
(open questions and items deferred.)

name: Church or Ministry Meeting
description: Ministry teams, elder/deacon boards, church staff.
instructions:
Write with warmth and clarity, appropriate for a church or ministry team.
Sections (use exactly these headings, in this order):
## Overview
(purpose of the gathering and a short summary.)
## Prayer Requests & Praises
(only if prayer requests, praises or pastoral concerns were shared; keep sensitive personal details brief and discreet.)
## Ministry Updates
(bullets grouped by ministry area (e.g., worship, youth, children, outreach, missions, facilities, finance) as discussed.)
## Discipleship & Spiritual Formation
(any discussion of discipleship, teaching, scripture or spiritual growth ("None mentioned." if absent).)
## Events & Calendar
(upcoming services, events, dates and volunteer needs mentioned.)
## Decisions
(bullets.)
## Action Items
(Markdown checklist with owner and due date when given.)
## Follow-Up & Care
(people or situations needing follow-up, as mentioned.)
## Scripture & Quotes
(scripture references and notable statements with timestamps, only if present.)

name: Creative Project Meeting
description: Design, content, media and production work.
instructions:
Sections (use exactly these headings, in this order):
## Project Snapshot
(the project, its goal and the current status as discussed.)
## Creative Direction
(vision, tone, style, audience, references and inspirations mentioned.)
## Feedback
(bullets of feedback given, grouped as **Keep**, **Change**, **Explore** where the transcript supports it.)
## Decisions
(bullets.)
## Deliverables & Owners
(Markdown table: Deliverable | Owner | Due | Status.)
## Open Creative Questions
(bullets.)
## Next Review
(next steps and review dates mentioned.)

name: Brainstorming Session
description: Captures every idea, then what rose to the top.
instructions:
Sections (use exactly these headings, in this order):
## Challenge
(the problem or question the group was brainstorming about.)
## All Ideas
(capture EVERY distinct idea raised, grouped under ### theme subheadings. Each idea as a bullet with a one-line description and who suggested it if a speaker label is available.)
## Most Promising Ideas
(ideas the group showed most energy for or agreed to pursue, with the reasons given.)
## Concerns & Constraints
(limitations, risks or objections raised.)
## Next Steps
(what will happen with the ideas, as mentioned.)

name: Interview Notes
description: Q&A format for interviews and conversations.
instructions:
Sections (use exactly these headings, in this order):
## Interview Overview
(who was interviewed (only names actually stated; otherwise use the speaker labels), the role or subject, and the purpose.)
## Questions & Answers
(for each main question: **Q:** the question (paraphrased) [timestamp], then **A:** a faithful summary of the answer with key specifics.)
## Key Insights
(the most important things learned.)
## Notable Quotes
(verbatim quotes with timestamps.)
## Strengths & Concerns
(only if evaluative points were explicitly discussed; otherwise "None mentioned.".)
## Follow-Up
(next steps mentioned.)

name: Lecture or Training Notes
description: Study notes for classes, sermons, trainings.
instructions:
Write as clear study notes.
Sections (use exactly these headings, in this order):
## Topic & Overview
(the subject and a short summary of the session.)
## Key Concepts
(each concept in **bold** with a concise explanation as presented.)
## Detailed Notes
(structured outline following the order of the session, using ### subheadings and nested bullets; include examples, definitions, steps and figures that were given.)
## Examples & Illustrations
(stories, examples or demonstrations used.)
## Key Takeaways
(3–7 bullets.)
## Review Questions
(3–5 questions a learner could use to review this material, answerable from the session content.)
## Assignments & Resources
(homework, readings, resources or deadlines mentioned.)

name: Detailed Minutes
instructions:
Write formal meeting minutes in the third person and past tense.
Sections (use exactly these headings, in this order):
## Meeting Details
(date, duration and attendees/speakers as listed in the meeting information (do not add others).)
## Call to Order & Opening
(how the meeting began, if discussed.)
## Agenda Items
(for each item in the order discussed: ### Item title [start timestamp], then **Discussion:** a factual paragraph; **Outcome:** the decision, motion or result (or "No decision recorded.").)
## Motions & Votes
(any motions, who moved/seconded and results, only if explicitly stated.)
## Action Items
(Markdown table: # | Action | Responsible | Due.)
## Next Meeting
(date/time if mentioned.)
## Adjournment
(if mentioned.)

name: Action Items Only
instructions:
Use only these sections (exactly these headings, in this order):
## Action Items
(a Markdown checklist. One line per task: "- [ ] **Task** — Owner: … — Due: … [timestamp]". Write "Owner: not specified" or "Due: not specified" when unknown. Order by due date when known, then by order discussed.)
## Waiting On / Dependencies
(tasks that depend on someone else or on a decision, if any.)
Do not include any other sections or commentary.
